title: align /v1/chat.completions stop semantics and stabilize streaming + function_call behavior
author: Anika Rao
description: Summary: This PR fixes several gaps in our OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer: correct stop token behavior across batch and streaming paths, ensure logprobs alignment when truncation occurs, and make function_call handling deterministic in streaming mode. Motivation: Customers hit parity mismatches when migrating from OpenAI endpoints — stop tokens could be applied at a different stage than OpenAI (sometimes after logprobs), streaming could emit partial assistant messages then abruptly close causing downstream parsers to mis-handle function_call signals, and multi-choice streaming with n>1 had racey ordering. We need deterministic, documented parity so apps relying on OpenAI semantics behave the same on Redwood. Design and changes: 1) Stop semantics: unify stop handling to apply token/sequence truncation before final logprob computation and chunk emission. This mirrors OpenAI behavior: the stop token(s) are removed from the output text and any token-level probabilities associated with the stopped token are excluded from returned logprobs. Implementation: added a StopProcessor that runs as the final step of the decode pipeline; it signals stream close and adjusts cached KV/logprob windows. 2) Streaming stability: replace ad-hoc stream-close signaling with a two-phase shutdown: a FIN intent message followed by an ack window to ensure consumers see final function_call blocks. This fixes observed race where library consumers missed the trailing "function_call" object. 3) Function calling parity: ensure function_call:{"name":"auto"/"none"/"<name>"} mapping is preserved in streaming partial events; the assistant role tokens used to decide function invocation are buffered and emitted only when the call is complete or when a stop triggers an early flush. 4) Logprobs alignment: when trim/truncate occurs due to stop or max_tokens limits, we drop logprob entries for removed tokens and adjust token_index mapping fields to match OpenAI responses. 5) n>1 streaming ordering: guarantee deterministic choice ordering by tagging each choice stream with choice_index and holding interleaved chunks until sequence alignment is resolved by the router. 6) Backwards compatibility: introduced a feature flag redwood.openai.compat.strict_parity (default true) to gate exact behavior; non-strict mode retains prior Redwood semantics for customers who depend on them. Tests & CI: added unit tests for StopProcessor, streaming integration tests that spawn two simulated clients and assert final assembled messages match OpenAI reference traces, and e2e coverage for function_call streaming under early stop conditions. A flaky test (stream_close_race) was stabilized by increasing the ack window timeout and adding deterministic sleeps to the integration harness; CI now passes. Files changed (high level): - api/openai_compat/handler.py: added StopProcessor integration and feature-flag checks - serving/streaming/stream_manager.py: two-phase stream shutdown and choice_index tagging - serving/streaming/tests/test_stream_stop.py: new unit/integration tests - api/openai_compat/logprob_adjuster.py: normalize logprobs after truncation - sdk/ts/openai_compat_client.ts: client-side partial-event schema docs and example - docs/openai-compat.md: documented new strict_parity flag and migration notes - tests/integration/function_call_stop_repro.py: reproducer and e2e assertions Commits (summary): 1) add StopProcessor and tests 2) implement two-phase streaming shutdown + choice_index 3) logprob trimming/normalization and mapping fixes 4) add feature flag + docs 5) fix failing integration test and CI flakes 6) squash/final cleanup Review thread (summary): - Liam: requested additional unit tests around logprob mapping for multi-byte utf8 sequences. Author: added tests (serving/streaming/tests/test_logprob_utf8.py). - Diego: flagged potential perf regression from StopProcessor copying buffers; asked for microbenchmark. Author: added microbenchmark and optimized to use zero-copy views where possible. - Maya: asked to surface the strict_parity flag in the Console UI flags page; created DES ticket (DES-87). QA: Verified streaming stability against recorded OpenAI traces (chat_stop_variant_{a,b,c}) and confirmed parity for stop/logprobs/function_call sequences. Migration notes: Operators should be aware of the new redwood.openai.compat.strict_parity flag; default true, no customer action required. If a customer relied on Redwood's previous, slightly different behavior, they can flip the flag to false while they adapt. Breaking changes: none by default; changing the flag can change output text/logprob deltas so call out in release notes. Checklist: - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration tests added - [x] docs updated - [x] benchmark added - [x] QA signoff Links: Linear ENG-2048 (design), SUP-431 (customer report), docs https://internal.redwood/docs/openai-compat#stop-and-function-calling Notes: The description intentionally keeps details high-level; see code for exact edge case handling. This PR was squashed on merge and the final commit message summarizes the changes for release notes.

review_comments: Liam: Please add a unit test that validates logprob index mapping with multi-byte UTF-8 tokens. Without it we risk off-by-one in some languages.
Anika: Added serving/streaming/tests/test_logprob_utf8.py that reproduces the UTF-8 case and asserts index mapping.
Diego: StopProcessor looks allocation-heavy; can we avoid copying the token window? Please add microbenchmark results.
Anika: Microbench added at tools/bench/stop_processor_bench.py and switched to zero-copy token views in the hot path.
Maya: Can Console expose the strict_parity flag? I'll file a DES ticket for UI changes.
Anika: Filed DES-87 and added docs note to docs/openai-compat.md
release_notes: Fix: OpenAI compat - stop tokens now truncate output before logprobs are computed; streaming no longer drops trailing function_call objects; deterministic ordering for n>1 streaming choices. Introduced redwood.openai.compat.strict_parity (default true) to toggle exact OpenAI parity. See docs/openai-compat.md for migration guidance.
